memory_candidates.content: In this repo's bash 5.3, a bare `declare -A arr` (no `=()` initializer) that never receives an element throws "unbound variable" under `set -u`/`set -uo pipefail` on a LATER `"${#arr[@]}"` (count) reference -- even though `"${!arr[@]}"` (key iteration) on the same never-populated array does NOT trigger it. This fires exactly in the common edge case where a detection loop legitimately finds zero matches (e.g. a validator check over a repo with zero occurrences of the field being checked). Fix: always initialize an associative array intended for a later `${#arr[@]}` check with an explicit `declare -A arr=()`, not a bare `declare -A arr` -- the explicit empty-array literal marks it "assigned" from declaration regardless of whether anything is later added to it.

Several agent-system core scripts (generate-todo.sh, generate-task-order.sh, check-task-references.sh) are gated by deploy-root-guard.sh / a structural deployed-tree check and refuse to run directly against the source store (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/**). When a task must verify a source-store-only edit to one of these scripts without deploying (e.g. because deploy is deliberately withheld during a multi-task concurrent cycle), build an isolated scratch directory shaped like a deployed tree -- mkdir -p <scratch>/.claude/scripts/lib, copy the edited script(s) plus their unchanged dependencies (deploy-root-guard.sh, lib/common.sh, and any sibling script they shell out to) into it, chmod +x, then invoke the script directly inside that scratch tree against a synthetic or copied-real state.json. This is the same contract test-generate-task-order.sh's own build_scratch() already uses, generalized to a manual, one-off verification.

A test suite's own candidate-resolution arrays for 'which copy of a dependency to use' (source-store vs. deployed) are not always internally consistent within the same file. test-validate-state.sh's drift-test block paired a deploy-first SCHEMA_CANDIDATES with a source-store-first WIDEN_VALIDATOR_CANDIDATES in the SAME check, which silently compared a stale deployed schema against a fresh source-store validator whenever deploy was withheld -- producing a false drift FAIL that looked like a real regression. When adding a new fixture/check to an existing test suite, grep the file for ALL of its *_CANDIDATES arrays and confirm they agree on source-store-first vs. deploy-first for the specific pairing your new check exercises, rather than assuming the whole file follows one convention.
